excerpt: A Kenya safari from Germany, planned in euros: the Frankfurt nonstop to Nairobi, eTA and insurance rules, German Foreign Office advice and three real Divulge itineraries.
content:
A Kenya safari from Germany starts with a nonstop Lufthansa flight from Frankfurt to Nairobi of about 8.5 hours, an online Kenya eTA and a private 7- to 10-day road safari through Amboseli, the Rift Valley lakes and the Masai Mara. Budget roughly €3,300-3,700 per person all in for a private week.

German travellers tend to plan carefully, and most price guides online are written in US dollars for Americans or in pounds for British readers. This guide converts the numbers into euros, explains the Frankfurt and Munich routings, sets out what the Auswärtiges Amt currently says about Kenya, and maps it all onto real Kenya safari packages run by our team in Nairobi.

Quick Facts

  • Nonstop flight: Lufthansa Frankfurt to Nairobi, daily, about 8 hours 30 minutes (schedule checked November 2026)
  • Beach gateway: Discover Airlines flies nonstop Frankfurt to Mombasa, about 8 hours 40 minutes
  • Entry: Kenya eTA for German passport holders, from US$30, plus mandatory Kenyan travel health insurance
  • Time difference: Kenya is 2 hours ahead of Germany in winter and 1 hour ahead in summer
  • Typical budget: about €3,300-3,700 per person for a private 7- to 10-day safari with flights
  • Best months: July to October for the migration; January to March for dry weather and lower rates

How Do You Fly From Germany to Nairobi?

The simplest start to a Kenya safari from Germany is the daily nonstop Lufthansa flight from Frankfurt, which takes about 8 hours 30 minutes. It leaves Frankfurt late morning and lands at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport around 22:00 local time, according to route schedules we checked in November 2026 (Lufthansa).

Because that flight lands late in the evening, we plan the first night at a hotel close to the airport or in Nairobi and start the game drives the next morning.

Flying from Munich, Hamburg, Berlin, Düsseldorf or Stuttgart

For a Kenya safari from Germany starting outside the Rhine-Main area, you usually connect. The common options are a short Lufthansa hop to Frankfurt, KLM through Amsterdam, or one-stop routings via Istanbul, the Gulf hubs or Addis Ababa. KLM's route page for Germany to Kenya listed return fares of roughly €700-765 from Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Düsseldorf and Stuttgart for summer travel when we checked in November 2026; treat these as indicative, since fares move daily.

Flying into Mombasa instead

Discover Airlines flies nonstop from Frankfurt to Mombasa on the Indian Ocean coast in about 8 hours 40 minutes. That suits a beach-first Kenya safari from Germany: a few days at Diani or Watamu, then Tsavo by road or a short flight to the Masai Mara.

What Does a Kenya Safari From Germany Cost in Euros?

A private 7-day Kenya safari from Germany costs roughly €3,300-3,400 per person all in, and a 10-day trip about €3,650-3,700, using our published starting prices, a return fare near €750, the eTA with insurance and guide tips. A shared 4-day budget safari comes to about €1,650.

Our trip prices are set in US dollars, so we converted them at the European Central Bank reference rate of 1 euro to US$1.0963 on 24 November 2026 (ECB euro reference rates). The table is a planning figure, not a quote: your bank's rate, your travel month and the lodges available all shift the final price.

For each Kenya safari from Germany in the table, the middle column assumes a €750 return fare, the eTA from US$30 plus the US$44 Kenyan health insurance premium (about €68 together), and US$10 per person per day in guide tips, which is the amount our trip pages suggest. Your own travel insurance is extra and depends on your age and policy.

What changes the price of a Kenya safari from Germany?

Three things move the bill most: the month, the lodge level and whether the vehicle is private. German summer school holidays fall inside the July to October migration, so August is the dearest month for flights and Mara camps. Our Kenya safari cost guide breaks the daily rate down by tier and season.

The Masai Mara hot air balloon flight is US$500 per person (about €456), and drinks are paid locally. Euro cash is less useful than US dollars on safari, so bring some clean, recent dollar notes for tips.

Which Itinerary Suits Travellers From Germany?

Most guests on a Kenya safari from Germany choose a private 7- to 10-day road safari, which fits a two-week holiday with travel days at each end. That length covers Amboseli for elephants below Kilimanjaro, the Rift Valley lakes and three nights in the Masai Mara without long drives every day.

Our 7-day Amboseli, Naivasha, Nakuru and Masai Mara safari is the route we suggest most often for a first Kenya safari from Germany. It includes a private Land Cruiser, full board, all park fees, a Lake Naivasha boat ride and a Maasai village visit.

Beach first or safari first?

If you fly into Mombasa, the 7-day Tsavo and Watamu bush and beach safari from US$1,970 per adult (about €1,797) keeps everything on the coast side, and the 3-day Masai Mara safari from Mombasa or Diani adds the Mara by light aircraft.

What Do German Citizens Need to Enter Kenya?

German citizens need a Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA), a passport valid for at least six months beyond the end of the stay and a return or onward ticket. The Auswärtiges Amt says to apply online no earlier than three months and no later than 72 hours before departure (checked November 2026).

The eTA starts at US$30 per traveller on the official Kenya eTA website (checked October 2026). Since early October 2026, a paid Kenyan travel health insurance policy must also be bought inside the eTA application, and the German Foreign Office notes that other insurers are not accepted for this requirement. Keep your own travel insurance as well, because the Kenyan policy does not cover cancellation or evacuation.

Before you book a Kenya safari from Germany, our Kenya eTA guide walks through the form step by step.

Is it safe to plan a Kenya safari from Germany right now?

The Auswärtiges Amt currently issues a partial travel warning (Teilreisewarnung) for Kenya, not a full one (German Foreign Office advice on Kenya, page dated 25 November 2026). The warning covers Mandera, Wajir, Garissa and Lamu counties, except Lamu and Manda islands, and it strongly advises against Baringo, West Pokot, Turkana, northern Tana River and the Moyale area.

None of these areas is on the circuit a Kenya safari from Germany usually follows: Amboseli, Naivasha, Nakuru and the Masai Mara. One practical point: Lake Bogoria lies in Baringo County, so while that advice stands we leave it out of German itineraries and use Lake Nakuru for flamingos instead. Our guide to safety on a Kenya safari covers the rest, and the same Foreign Office page also warned of heavy rain from October to December 2026.

Vaccinations and malaria

No yellow fever certificate is needed when you fly directly from Germany, but you need one if you arrive from a country with yellow fever risk; our yellow fever requirements page explains the rule. Malaria risk is rated high in most of Kenya, including safari areas and the coast, and low in Nairobi city (NHS Fit for Travel, checked November 2026).

For any Kenya safari from Germany, book a consultation with a travel medicine doctor (Reisemediziner) six to eight weeks before you fly, and read our Kenya safari vaccinations guide beforehand so you know what to ask.

When Is the Best Time for a Kenya Safari From Germany?

The best time for a Kenya safari from Germany is July to October, when the Great Migration is usually in the Masai Mara, or January to March, when the weather is dry and rates are lower. Kenya is 2 hours ahead of Germany in winter and 1 hour in summer, so jet lag is mild.

How Do You Book a Private Safari With a Nairobi Operator?

Booking a Kenya safari from Germany with a Nairobi operator means you book your own flight in Germany and we arrange everything from the airport onward: transfers, lodges, park fees, the vehicle and your guide. You get one written quote in US dollars that lists every lodge and what is included.

Send us your flight times as soon as you hold them, because the late Frankfurt arrival shapes the first night. Tell us about languages too: our driver guides work in English, and we can tell you which bilingual guides are free for your dates when you enquire.

Insider Tips

  • Fly Frankfurt nonstop: the daily direct flight saves a connection and lands in time for a night's sleep before day one
  • Pay attention to bag weight: fly-in add-ons usually allow 15 kg in a soft bag, far less than your long-haul allowance
  • Carry US dollars: small, recent notes for tips; euros are harder to use in the bush
  • Apply early: apply once flights are fixed, up to three months ahead
  • Watch the Bundesland calendar: your state's summer holiday dates decide whether you catch peak migration or the cheaper shoulder

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a direct flight from Germany to Kenya?

Yes. Lufthansa flies nonstop from Frankfurt to Nairobi daily in about 8 hours 30 minutes, landing around 22:00, and Discover Airlines flies nonstop from Frankfurt to Mombasa in about 8 hours 40 minutes. From Munich, Berlin, Hamburg and other German airports you connect, usually through Frankfurt, Amsterdam or a Gulf hub. Schedules change, so confirm when you book.

How much does a Kenya safari from Germany cost?

A Kenya safari from Germany costs about €1,650 per person for a 4-day shared budget trip and roughly €3,300-3,700 for a private 7- to 10-day safari, including a return flight near €750, the eTA with Kenyan health insurance and guide tips. Prices rise in August and over Christmas, and your own travel insurance is extra.

Do Germans need a visa for Kenya?

Germans do not need a traditional visa but must hold a Kenya eTA before flying. It costs from US$30, and since October 2026 a mandatory Kenyan travel health insurance policy is bought during the same application. Apply no earlier than three months and no later than 72 hours before departure, with a passport valid six months beyond your stay.

What is the best month for a Kenya safari from Germany?

August and September are the best months for the Great Migration in the Masai Mara and fit German summer school holidays, but they are the busiest and dearest. February is a strong alternative for a winter escape: dry weather, good game viewing and lower rates. October often still has the migration with fewer visitors.

How many days do you need for a Kenya safari?

Seven to ten days on the ground suits most travellers from Germany. Seven days covers Amboseli, Lake Naivasha, Lake Nakuru and three nights in the Masai Mara, and ten days adds slower days and a night in Nairobi. With a daytime Frankfurt flight, a two-week holiday leaves room for a few beach days on the coast.

Final Thoughts

A Kenya safari from Germany is easier than many people expect: one nonstop flight from Frankfurt, an online eTA and a private week in the parks, for roughly €3,300-3,700 per person. Fix your holiday dates first, because they decide the season, the price and how early you need to book.
